Kishore, sit. You're asking me why your aunt and I nearly separated when you were small? You're old enough now. When I was twenty-five, two years married, I had an affair with a woman at my office. Three months. I'm Ujjwal, your uncle, and I'm not proud of any of it.

When it ended, I was torn in pieces. Shame, yes. But also excuses: she was busy with her mother, she didn't understand me. And fear, every day, that she'd find out.

One night I nearly said to her, "You pushed me to it." I heard how ugly it was before it left my mouth.

So I told her the truth, all of it, without blaming her. She cried and shouted and left for her sister's. I didn't ask her to comfort me, though I wanted to. I went to a counsellor alone. It took four years before she trusted me again. That was the price, and it was fair.

Imran asked to see me alone. For five months he has been lying to his wife, Farida, about Saturday mornings. He tells her he plays cricket. In fact he has been meeting his father, from whom Farida's family asked him to cut ties after a bitter property dispute. He deletes the call logs.

We discussed that concealment often slowly deadens a bond, and that honesty, even when it costs something, gives the partner a real choice. We planned how he might tell Farida: plainly, without blaming her family, and ready to hear her anger.

passage:
Raghav, you asked what the fight with my husband was about. It's Swati, and I'll be honest because I need to say it to someone. For a year I'd been hiding money. Not stealing, just a separate savings account from my salary, in my own name. I never told him. I told myself it was because he spends carelessly and would want to use it. Really, I was scared of how he'd react.

Then last week he found the bank letter in my cupboard. He wasn't even angry about the money. He was hurt that I'd hidden it. "What else don't I know?" That's what stung.

I realised the hiding did more damage than the money ever could.

So I sat with him and showed him everything. I said why I'd felt I needed it. Then I asked if we could plan together what's shared and what's personal. We're seeing a financial counsellor next month to work it out properly.

qa.q: How did Swati's husband feel when he found the letter?
